De [[fn-aplicaciones|una variable]] vien: From [[fn-aplicaciones|one variable]] comes the recipe: differentiate, set to zero, check. From the previous topic, the gradient and its key property: it points uphill. With the two together you optimise in several variables, and when the equations refuse to be solved, with the second alone you build the algorithm that trains neural networks.
Ya sabes optimizar funciones de una vari: You already know how to optimise functions of one variable: differentiate, set to zero, check. With several variables the setup is the same, but a new problem appears: the equations that come out are usually impossible to solve by hand. And out of that difficulty was born the algorithm that today trains every artificial intelligence on the planet.
En un máximo o un mínimo, la superficie: At a maximum or a minimum, the surface is horizontal in every direction. That is, the gradient vanishes.
\\nabla f(a,b) = \\vec{0} \\iff \\frac{\: \nabla f(a,b) = \vec{0} \iff \frac{\partial f}{\partial x} = 0 \ \text{ and } \ \frac{\partial f}{\partial y} = 0
El $\\iff$ es «si y solo si» y $\\vec{0}:
The $\iff$ is “if and only if” and $\vec{0}$ is “the zero vector”, the one all of whose components are zero.

Read as: “the gradient of f at the point a, b is the zero vector if and only if the partial derivative with respect to x and the partial derivative with respect to y are both zero”.

It is the two-variable version of “the derivative vanishes”: at a maximum or a minimum the ground is level in every direction at once, not just in one.
Pero, igual que en una variable, que el: But, just as with one variable, the gradient vanishing is not enough. Here there are three possibilities instead of two, and the new one is the interesting one:
sube en unas y baja en otras: it rises in some and falls in others
El punto de silla no tiene equivalente e: The saddle point has no equivalent in one variable, and it is the reason optimising in many dimensions is hard. In spaces of millions of dimensions —like those of a neural network— saddle points are far more plentiful than minima.
En $f(x, y) = x^2 - y^2$ el gradiente se: In $f(x, y) = x^2 - y^2$ the gradient vanishes at $(0, 0)$, and $f(0, 0) = 0$. Is it a minimum?
Sí: el gradiente es cero y en $x$ la fun: Yes: the gradient is zero and along $x$ the function rises
Sube por el eje $x$, pero por el eje $y$: It rises along the $x$ axis, but along the $y$ axis it falls: $f(0, 1) = -1 < 0$. A minimum has to rise in every direction.
No: es un punto de silla: No: it is a saddle point
Sube en unas direcciones y baja en otras: It rises in some directions and falls in others. Zero gradient is a necessary condition, not a sufficient one, just like $f'(a) = 0$ in one variable.
No se puede saber sin la segunda derivad: There is no way to tell without the second derivative
Aquí se puede saber probando dos direcci: Here you can tell by trying two directions: $f(1, 0) = 1 > 0$ and $f(0, 1) = -1 < 0$. With that it can no longer be either a minimum or a maximum.
Un mínimo a mano y después a pasitos: A minimum by hand and then in small steps
Hallar el mínimo de $f(x, y) = x^2 + y^2: Find the minimum of $f(x, y) = x^2 + y^2 - 2x - 4y + 5$. Then apply two steps of gradient descent from $(0, 0)$ with $\eta = 0{.}25$.
<strong>Punto crítico.</strong> $f_x = 2: Critical point. $f_x = 2x - 2 = 0$ and $f_y = 2y - 4 = 0$: the only candidate is $(1, 2)$.
Dos parciales, dos ecuaciones. ¿Qué punt: Two partials, two equations. What point comes out?
<strong>Tipo.</strong> Completando cuadr: Type. Completing squares, $f = (x - 1)^2 + (y - 2)^2$: a sum of two squares, it rises in every direction. A minimum, with value $f(1, 2) = 0$.
Escribe $f$ como suma de cuadrados. ¿Qué: Write $f$ as a sum of squares. What sign does each have?
<strong>Primer paso.</strong> En $(0, 0): First step. At $(0, 0)$, $\nabla f = (-2, -4)$. New point: $(0, 0) - 0{.}25\cdot(-2, -4) = (0{.}5,\ 1)$. It has moved towards the minimum: against the gradient.
El gradiente en el origen apunta hacia f: The gradient at the origin points out of the bowl. Which way does the step go?
<strong>Segundo paso.</strong> En $(0{,}: Second step. At $(0{.}5, 1)$, $\nabla f = (-1, -2)$. New point: $(0{.}5, 1) + 0{.}25\cdot(1, 2) = (0{.}75,\ 1{.}5)$. The distance to $(1, 2)$ has again been halved.
<strong>Por qué a la mitad.</strong> Cad: Why halved. Each component does $x_{n+1} - 1 = (1 - 2\eta)(x_n - 1) = \frac{1}{2}(x_n - 1)$. With $\eta = 0{.}5$ it would arrive in one step; with $\eta = 1$, the factor would be $-1$: it would oscillate without ever getting closer.
¿Qué $\\eta$ llevaría al mínimo en un so: What $\eta$ would reach the minimum in a single step? And which one would make the point oscillate?
Con la fórmula, el mínimo sale exacto. C: With the formula, the minimum comes out exact. With the small steps, it comes out approximate but without solving any equation: it is what is done when there are a million variables and the equations refuse.
Si no se puede resolver $\\nabla f = \\v: If $\nabla f = \vec 0$ cannot be solved, this is what is done: start at any point and go down. Which way? Towards where you descend most, which is exactly the direction opposite to the gradient.
La letra $\\eta$ es la eta griega y aquí:
The letter $\eta$ is the Greek eta and here it is read “learning rate”: it is how long each step you take is.

It is said: “x sub n plus one equals x sub n minus eta times the gradient of f evaluated at x sub n”.

Translated: “my next position is the current one, taking a step of size eta in the direction opposite to the gradient”. Opposite because the gradient points to where it rises, and here we want to go down.
El número $\\eta$ es la <strong>tasa de: The number $\eta$ is the learning rate: the size of the step. And choosing it well is the whole art of the method.
Bajar la ladera a pasitos: Going down the hillside in small steps
Haz clic en cualquier punto para soltar: Click anywhere to drop the ball. Change the size of the step and watch what happens when it is too small or too large.
En el cuenco alargado, ¿la bola irá rect: On the elongated bowl, will the ball go straight to the centre or zigzag? And if you raise $\eta$ to 1.8, will it arrive faster or stop arriving at all?
Un cuenco alargado. Con un solo mínimo,: An elongated bowl. With a single minimum, the descent always ends up finding it.
Punto de silla en el origen: sube en una: A saddle point at the origin: it rises in one direction and falls in the other. The descent dodges it and goes off down the valley.
Dos mínimos separados por una loma. A cu: Two minima separated by a ridge. Which one you reach depends only on where you start: that is a local minimum.
<strong>muy pequeña</strong>, avanza a p: very small, it advances at a snail's pace and needs a great many iterations.
<strong style=\"color:var(--bad)\">demas: too large: the steps overshoot and the path oscillates or blows up.
reasonable: it converges in a few steps.
converge, pero tarda una eternidad: it converges, but takes an eternity
baja rápido y se asienta en el mínimo: it goes down fast and settles at the minimum
Ajustar $\\eta$ es el problema práctico: Tuning $\eta$ is problem number one in practical machine learning. There are methods that change it as they go (Adam, RMSprop), but the underlying idea is still this same two-line formula.
El descenso de gradiente es el algoritmo: Gradient descent is the algorithm that trains every artificial intelligence model in existence, without exception. The idea is exactly that of going down a mountain in fog: look at the slope under your feet and take a step downwards. What changes from one model to another is the size of the step, which is the same dilemma you see here: too short and you never arrive, too long and you overshoot in leaps.
El descenso de gradiente es <strong>cieg: Gradient descent is blind: it sees only the slope beneath it. If it falls into a valley, it stays there even if there is a deeper valley on the other side of the ridge.
En una variable esto se arregla estudian: With one variable this is fixed by studying the whole function. With a million variables that cannot be done, so tricks are used: starting at several different places, or the two ideas of the next section, which also solve another much bigger problem.
Minilotes: el gradiente como una encuest: Minibatches: the gradient as an opinion poll
Hay un problema de tamaño que la fórmula: There is a problem of size that the formula hides. The function being minimised is almost always a sum over the data: the error of the first, plus that of the second, plus that of the third. With a million data, each step of the descent requires going through all of them to compute a single gradient. Taking a thousand steps would cost a thousand million computations.
La salida es la de [[pe-inferencia|el mu: The way out is that of [[pe-inferencia|sampling]]: to know what a country thinks you do not ask everybody, you ask a thousand people. The same here. A handful of data is taken at random —a minibatch—, the gradient is computed with them alone and the step is taken. That gradient is not the true one: it is an estimate of it, and like every estimate of a mean, it is unbiased and its error shrinks like the root of the sample size.
Se lee: <em>«el gradiente se aproxima po:
Read as: “the gradient is approximated by one over m, times the sum of the gradients of the data in the batch”.

The important part is the $\frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}$: going from 100 to 10,000 data per batch reduces the error only to a tenth, but costs a hundred times more. That is why it pays to take many steps with a mediocre gradient rather than few with an exact one.
El ruido de la estimación no es solo un: The noise of the estimate is not merely a lesser evil: it helps. A slightly wrong gradient at each step keeps the ball from sitting still in any small hollow, and it is one of the reasons stochastic descent finds better solutions than the exact one on big problems.
El otro problema es la forma del terreno: The other problem is the shape of the ground. In a long narrow valley, the gradient points mostly towards the walls and very little along the floor: the descent bounces from side to side and advances slowly in the direction that matters. You saw it in the demo of the elongated bowl.
La cura es darle <strong>inercia</strong: The cure is to give it inertia. Instead of each step depending only on the gradient right now, a velocity is carried along that accumulates the previous steps. The components that change sign at each bounce cancel one another, and the one that always points the same way adds up and grows.
Se leen: <em>«uve sub ene más uno es bet:
They read: “v sub n plus one is beta times v sub n, minus eta times the gradient” and “x sub n plus one is x sub n plus v sub n plus one”.

$\beta$ is the momentum, between 0 and 1, and it says how much velocity is kept from one step to the next. With $\beta = 0$ it is the usual descent. With $\beta = 0{.}9$, a constant gradient ends up taking steps ten times longer, because $1 + \beta + \beta^2 + \dots = \frac{1}{1-\beta}$: it is the sum of [[fn-sucesiones|a geometric progression]].
Con inercia y sin ella, en el mismo vall: With inertia and without it, in the same valley
Las dos bolas salen del mismo sitio en u: The two balls set off from the same place in a narrow valley. The blue one is the usual descent; the orange one carries momentum. Raise the momentum little by little and watch the sideways bounces cancel while the advance along the floor accumulates.
El valle es estrecho de lado y largo de: The valley is narrow across and long along. With high momentum, which do you think will cancel first: the sideways swaying or the advance along it?
Un valle alargado con dos trayectorias d: An elongated valley with two descent paths, one without momentum and one with momentum
Con tanta inercia la bola ya no frena a: With so much inertia the ball no longer brakes in time and overshoots: momentum can be overdone too.
La inercia gana: el vaivén lateral se ca: Inertia wins: the sideways swaying cancels by itself and the advance along the floor accumulates.
Con poco momento apenas hay diferencia:: With little momentum there is hardly any difference: the velocity has to get a chance to accumulate.
¿Por qué el momento acelera en un valle: Why does momentum speed things up in a long narrow valley?
Porque los rebotes laterales cambian de: Because the sideways bounces change sign and cancel as they accumulate, while the advance along the floor always points the same way and adds up
La velocidad es una media de los gradien: The velocity is an average of the recent gradients. What oscillates averages out to almost zero; what is constant accumulates up to $\frac{1}{1-\beta}$ times the normal step.
Porque aumenta la tasa de aprendizaje en: Because it raises the learning rate equally in every direction
Si fuera por igual no arreglaría nada: e: If it were equal it would fix nothing: the problem is precisely that you need to advance a lot in one direction and little in another. What momentum does is tell them apart by itself.
Porque calcula el gradiente con más prec: Because it computes the gradient more accurately
El gradiente es el mismo. Lo que cambia: The gradient is the same. What changes is how those of several consecutive steps are combined.
Entrenar una red neuronal es exactamente: Training a neural network is exactly this and nothing more than this:
Los <strong>parámetros</strong> de la re: The parameters of the network (there may be thousands of millions) are the coordinates of the point.
La <strong>función de pérdida</strong> m: The loss function measures how badly the network predicts: it is the surface to be descended.
El <strong>gradiente</strong> se calcula: The gradient is computed with the chain rule, applied layer by layer. That is called backpropagation.
Y se dan pasitos, millones de veces, has: And small steps are taken, millions of times, until the loss stops going down.
Merece la pena detenerse aquí. Todo el a: It is worth pausing here. All of deep learning —language models, image recognition, self-driving cars— rests on two things you already know: the chain rule and the idea that the gradient points to the steepest slope. The power does not come from more sophisticated mathematics, but from applying this at an enormous scale. If you want to see that claim worked out in full, with the vocabulary and the examples, start with [[ia-que-es|learning is adjusting numbers]]: there this very computation is done by hand on a line and then left to run by itself.
De la regla de la cadena a la IA: From the chain rule to AI
Cauchy propuso el método en 1847 para re: Cauchy proposed the method in 1847 to solve systems of equations in astronomy. For more than a century it was just another numerical technique, honest and unremarkable. In 1986 Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams combined it with backpropagation to train neural networks, and even so another twenty-five years —and graphics cards— were needed for the method to show what it was capable of.
